TOP STORYLINE (a correction to yesterday's record): the GA4-audit stranded-commit pattern that 08-27's QA session declared FIXED was a false negative. Read the real cron log (~/.claude/ga4-audit-cron.log) via Desktop Commander (real Mac shell, not this session's sandbox) rather than trusting a single sync-check snapshot, and found ALL THREE cron runs since the e04cccec PATH fix landed (08-26, 08-27, 08-28 mornings, each 09:45 AEST) failed to push, every one with the identical new signature 'fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured' -- notably NOT the old 'gh: command not found' error, which confirms the PATH fix genuinely resolved gh-resolution but exposed a second, previously-masked failure underneath it. Reproduced gh's credential helper directly with `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com

' | env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$HOME/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" git credential fill` from an interactive Desktop-Commander-spawned shell -- it SUCCEEDED (returned a real token, gh reports the store as 'keyring'), meaning the failure is not PATH, not HOME, not the credential-helper resolution itself, but something specific to the true cron daemon's execution context that this interactive-shell repro could not reproduce. Checked `crontab -l`: the GA4 job runs via classic BSD `cron` ('45 9 * * * bash .../ga4-audit-cron.sh'), not a launchd agent. This is the textbook shape of a well-known macOS gotcha: plain `cron` jobs execute outside the user's login/GUI security session and commonly cannot access Keychain-backed credential stores (gh's token here is stored via the system keyring) even though the identical command works fine from any real interactive shell (Terminal, SSH, or this session's Desktop-Commander shell) -- which explains why every manual repro attempt looks fine while the actual unattended cron keeps failing. This also retroactively explains 08-27's false-positive: something OTHER than the cron's own push (source not identified -- not this session, not the cron's own heal-fallback, both of which are logged as failing that morning) must have pushed 529cee52 to origin between the cron's 09:45 AEST failure and the QA session's ~12:06 PM AEST sync check that day; the log proves the automated path did not do it, so the 08-27 'first day the fix was live' claim was incorrect and should not have been marked FIXED. This is the same 'QA session's own push as incidental safety net' pattern documented on 08-24 through 08-26, just executed via Desktop Commander instead of this session's own sandboxed bash (which has no gh binary at all, confirmed via `which gh` returning empty -- a separate, expected limitation of this Linux sandbox, distinct from the real Mac's cron-vs-interactive-shell Keychain gap). Real fix still needed from the founder: either store the GitHub token outside Keychain for cron's use (a plaintext token file read via GH_TOKEN env var in the crontab line, avoiding gh's keyring lookup entirely) or convert the crontab entry to a launchd LaunchAgent (which typically retains login-session Keychain access). regression_matrix.title: Autoposter's GA4-audit commit stranded unpushed -- 08-27's 'FIXED' call was a false negative; the pattern recurred on all 3 cron runs since the PATH fix, for a DIFFERENT underlying reason
regression_matrix.evidence: CORRECTION to yesterday's record: 08-27's QA session verified 'local HEAD 0 ahead/0 behind origin/main at session start' and concluded the e04cccec PATH fix was working end-to-end. It was not -- the cron's OWN log (~/.claude/ga4-audit-cron.log, read directly via Desktop Commander this run, not available to the sandboxed bash used on 08-27) shows the 08-27 09:45 AEST cron run's push AND its own stranded-commit heal-fallback both failed that morning, with the identical error the 08-26 run got ('fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured'). The 08-28 09:45 AEST run failed the same way a third time. Something other than the automated cron path pushed 529cee52 to origin between the 08-27 cron's failure and that day's QA sync-check ~2.3 hours later -- source not identified, but definitively not the cron itself per its own log. Root-cause correction: the PATH fix DID work (the specific 'gh: command not found' sub-message is absent from all 3 post-fix log entries, confirming gh now resolves) but exposed a second, deeper failure underneath: reproducing gh's credential helper from an interactive shell with the cron's exact PATH succeeded cleanly (real token returned), while `crontab -l` confirms this job runs via classic BSD cron (not launchd) -- the textbook macOS condition where cron jobs run outside the login/GUI security session and cannot access Keychain-backed credentials (gh's token store here is 'keyring') even though the identical command works from any interactive shell. This session pushed the 08-28 stranded commit (9c1725a1) via Desktop Commander's real shell (working gh auth there) as an immediate stopgap -- verified 0 ahead/0 behind after.
regression_matrix.recommendation: The PATH fix (e04cccec) should stay -- it resolved a real, separate problem. A second fix is now needed for the Keychain-access gap: either (a) store the GitHub token outside Keychain for cron's use, e.g. a plaintext token file the crontab line exports as GH_TOKEN so `gh`/git credential resolution never needs the keyring, or (b) migrate this crontab entry to a launchd LaunchAgent, which typically retains login-session Keychain access. Until one of these lands, expect this exact stranded-commit symptom to recur every morning and to require either a manual push or an incidental QA-session push to clear -- do not re-mark this FIXED on the strength of a single clean sync-check again; check the cron's own log first.

new_findings_today.title: GA4-audit stranded-commit pattern is NOT fixed -- it recurred on all 3 cron runs since the PATH fix, root cause is cron's lack of Keychain access (not PATH); 08-27's 'FIXED' verdict was a false negative and is corrected here
new_findings_today.detail: See run.executor and the NEW-2026-08-26-002 regression_matrix entry (updated to REGRESSION today) for the full investigation. Summary: the cron log itself (not available to the 08-27 session, which only checked git sync state) shows the 08-26, 08-27, and 08-28 morning cron runs ALL failed to push, each with 'fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured' -- a different, new error from the pre-fix 'gh: command not found'. This confirms the e04cccec PATH fix genuinely resolved gh-resolution but did not fix the underlying push capability; a second failure (cron's inability to access the macOS Keychain where gh stores its auth token, a known limitation of classic BSD cron vs. launchd) was masked underneath it and is now the active blocker. Pushed today's stranded commit (9c1725a1) as an immediate stopgap via Desktop Commander (which has working gh auth in its interactive-shell context, unlike both the cron and this session's own sandboxed bash tool, which has no gh binary at all).
new_findings_today.evidence:
~/.claude/ga4-audit-cron.log, read via Desktop Commander: 08-26 09:45:14 entry shows 'gh auth git-credential get: gh: command not found' then push failure; 08-27 09:45:13 and 08-28 09:45:10 entries show push failure WITHOUT that sub-message, both ending 'fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured'. `printf 'protocol=https
host=github.com

' | env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$HOME/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" git credential fill` from an interactive Desktop-Commander shell succeeded (returned a real token; `gh auth status` shows 'Logged in ... (keyring)'). `crontab -l` shows '45 9 * * * bash ".../ga4-audit-cron.sh" >> ...' -- classic cron, no launchd agent found for this job. `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...main` was '0  1' (1 ahead) at session start, '0  0' after this session's `git push origin main` via Desktop Commander.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Store the GitHub token outside Keychain for cron's specific use (a plaintext token file, exported as GH_TOKEN in the crontab line or sourced at the top of ga4-audit-cron.sh) so credential resolution never depends on Keychain access from a non-GUI-session process -- or migrate the crontab entry to a launchd LaunchAgent. Re-verify by checking the cron log directly the morning after any fix lands, not just a same-day git-sync snapshot (which is exactly what produced 08-27's false negative).

new_findings_today.title: newsletter_events received its first row -- a real, signature-verified Resend webhook event from an apparently-unrelated 'Manifestation OS' sender sharing the same Resend account/domain as NakshIQ's newsletter

Two implications: positively, this confirms RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is configured in production and the webhook is registered in Resend's dashboard (the route's fail-closed design, confirmed by reading source on 08-27, would not have written a row otherwise) -- resolving 08-27's open verification question. Separately, it suggests a second, apparently-unrelated product ('Manifestation OS') is sending mail through the same Resend account and possibly the same registered webhook URL, so its delivery events land inside NakshIQ's own newsletter_events table. This may be entirely intentional (a founder consolidating personal-project infra), but is worth a conscious decision either way, since the table's stated purpose is per-recipient delivery observability for NakshIQ's own newsletter specifically.

If NakshIQ-only delivery metrics matter here, consider either a separate Resend webhook endpoint/secret for the other product, or a filter in the ingestion route keyed on sender/tag. Worth pairing with the still-open deal_radar-schema founder decision (NEW-2026-08-25-002) since both are the same underlying question: which other products intentionally share this project's infrastructure.

honest_caveats: TOP STORYLINE: 08-27's QA session incorrectly declared the GA4-audit stranded-commit pattern FIXED. It was not -- the cron's own log (read this run via Desktop Commander, not available to the 08-27 session's sandboxed bash) shows all 3 runs since the PATH fix (08-26, 08-27, 08-28 mornings) failed to push, with a NEW error signature distinct from the pre-fix one. Root cause identified as cron's lack of macOS Keychain access for gh's stored credentials (classic BSD cron vs. launchd), not PATH. Pushed today's stranded commit as an immediate stopgap. See NEW-2026-08-28-001 and the corrected NEW-2026-08-26-002 regression_matrix entry. Lesson for future sessions: verify a 'fix' by reading the actual cron/job log, not by checking git-sync state alone -- something else can silently paper over a still-broken automated path.
